title: dam config list answer
description: What dam config list prints on standard output with -o: where the two files are and every setting dam is using. A secret is never shown. A file that does not read gives the error document instead.

config.description: The path of config.lua, or null when there is none.

secrets.description: The path of secrets.lua, beside config.lua, or null when there is none.

project.description: Inside a project, its .dam.lua and every setting it holds, all from the project; null outside one or when the file does not load.

hooks_from.description: Where that switch comes from: this clone's own record, project.hooks in config.lua, or neither.

done_children.description: What dam done --force does with open children of a task under path: up, keep or into:<name>; null when unset.

warnings.description: Each token dam ignores or holds disabled, as dam doctor warns of it, and a project .dam.lua that does not load. Without -o each goes to standard error.

setting.description: One setting, or a part holding settings by name, as dam config get prints it with -o json. A leaf is the object whose default is a boolean, a hidden credential is the object whose hidden is a boolean, and a filter's match function or a hook's run function is the object whose function is a boolean; any other object is a part, and a part may hold settings named value, default, hidden or function.

hidden.description: A credential, whose value is never shown. function is true for one dam calls when the remote is used, and false for one written as text.

function.description: A filter's match function or a hook's run function, whose source is never shown.

value.description: The value. A list holds texts, or for a token's grant one object per grant as dam token list prints it. A disabled token reads disabled. It is null for a setting dam knows that the file leaves without a value and that has no default.

default.description: True when the file does not set it: dam then uses its own default, or nothing when value is null.
